newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Ostracised Islamic sect to boycott Pakistan poll.
newsitem.headline: Ostracised Islamic sect to boycott Pakistan poll.

text.p: An ostracised Islamic sect said on Tuesday it would boycott general elections in Pakistan set for February 3 and would not make use of the minority quota of seats reserved for it.

A spokesman for the Ahmadi sect, Malik Khalid Masood, in an advertisement published in a newspaper, said his community considered it against their conscience and faith to take up the non-Moslem seats reserved for the Ahmadis.

A 1974 Pakistani constitutional amendment declared Ahmadis outside the pale of Islam and gave them a minority status. But the Ahmadis have termed this discrimination and a violation of fundamental human rights.

"Since Ahmadis have not enlisted themselves as voters, there is no Ahmadi constituency... During all the previous elections this fact has been recorded time and again that Ahmadis do not wish to avail these seats," he said.
He said the chief election commissioner had been given the Ahmadis' position by written representation.
"Election of these seats is a negation of the very principle of representation, a violence to spirit of the constitution and an outrage to justice, fairplay and fundmental human rights."

The Ahmadis say that although they were declared non-Moslems in 1974, their real persecution began after late General Mohammad Zia-ul-Haq seized power in a 1977 military coup and started a campaign to "Islamise" Pakistan.
The Ahmadis are estimated to number about four million out of Pakistan's 120 million people and more than 10 million worldwide.
